files.lesson.md: --- order: 8 unit: powers9 node: AC9M9A01 n2 uses: [AC9M9A01 n1, AC9M8N02 n2] assumes: [AC9M8N02 n1, AC9M8N02 n2] connection: kilo-mega-giga title: All the index laws summary: "The index laws still work with zero and negative indices: add when multiplying, subtract when dividing, multiply for a power of a power. Be careful subtracting a negative." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "How many photos fit on a phone? The answer comes from a division of two powers of 10." app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8345 url: http://127.0.0.1:8345/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: laws.yml#explain-pic, caption: "$10^3 \\div 10^6$: three pairs cancel and three 10s are left underneath: $10^{-3}$, a thousandth." } explainClip: query: { code: "@laws.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Same laws, any indices" say: "The laws are the same. Subtract the indices, even if the answer goes negative." clip: - caption: { text: "2² ÷ 2²: everything cancels. 2⁰ = 1.", say: "Two squared over two squared cancels to one." } - click: Make the second index bigger - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "2² ÷ 2³: 2 − 3 = −1, so 2⁻¹.", say: "Two minus three is minus one, so two to the minus one." } - click: Make the second index bigger - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "2² ÷ 2⁴: 2 − 4 = −2, so 2⁻².", say: "Two minus four is minus two." } - wait: 800 --- In Year 8 you added and subtracted indices. The same laws work when the answer is zero or negative. ## Predict: photos on a phone ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a number of photos shows who loses track of how many zeros come from dividing powers of 10." check: type: predict q: "A phone has 128 gigabytes of storage and each photo is 4 megabytes. How many photos fit?" options: - "32 000" - "32" - "320 000" - "3 200 000" actual: "32 000. 128 GB is 128 × 10⁹ bytes and 4 MB is 4 × 10⁶ bytes. 128 ÷ 4 = 32 and 10⁹ ÷ 10⁶ = 10³, so 32 × 10³ = 32 000." ``` No calculator. How many photos fit? ## Run: bigger over smaller ```step stage: run insight: "A kilobyte over a megabyte divides two powers of 10: the index goes negative, because the kilobyte is the smaller one." try: { playground: board, starter: "laws.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Set the board to $10^3 \\div 10^6$: a kilobyte as a fraction of a megabyte. What's left underneath?", when: "m = 3 and n = 6" } ``` Move $m$ and $n$. Look at the index of the answer, and what it means. ## Investigate: all the laws ```step stage: investigate insight: "The laws are the same for any indices; the care is in the signs. Jo subtracts the size of a negative index instead of subtracting the negative." tasks: - check: type: number q: "Simplify $2^{-3} \\times 2^{5}$. It's 2 to what power?" answer: 2 explain: "Multiplying adds the indices: −3 + 5 = 2, so 2²." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#jo" text: "Jo simplifies $5^6 \\div 5^{-2}$. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: subtract-negative-index explain: "Line 3: 6 − (−2) = 6 + 2 = 8. Subtracting a negative adds, so it's 5⁸." - check: type: question q: "What is $(4 \\times 10^{-3}) \\times (2 \\times 10^{5})$?" options: ["$8 \\times 10^{2}$", "$8 \\times 10^{-15}$", "$6 \\times 10^{2}$", "$8 \\times 10^{8}$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Add the indices, don't multiply them: −3 + 5 = 2.", "Multiply 4 and 2, don't add them.", "−3 + 5 = 2, not 8."] explain: "4 × 2 = 8 and 10⁻³ × 10⁵ = 10²." ``` ### Add the indices Here's the routine with negatives in it. ```worked (2^{-2})^3 \times 2^9 \div 2^{-1} :: Powers of powers first. = 2^{-6} \times 2^9 \div 2^{-1} :: −2 × 3 = −6. = 2^{3} \div 2^{-1} :: Multiply: −6 + 9 = 3. = 2^{3 - (-1)} :: Divide: subtract the index. = 2^4 = 16 :: 3 − (−1) = 4. ``` Now try one on paper: $5^{-3} \times 5^7 \div 5^2$. Then type the value. ### Find the mistake Read Jo's working. What's $6 - (-2)$? ### Scientific style ## Modify: change the indices ```step stage: modify insight: "Changing the base, the signs and the power of a power: the same laws, with care over negative indices and a zero index." try: { playground: board, starter: "laws.yml#vary", height: 620 } tasks: - hint: ["Set a to 2, m to 3 and n to 5.", "Subtract the indices: 3 − 5."] check: { type: answer, q: "Work out $2^3 \\div 2^5$ as a fraction.", answer: "1/4", form: simplest, feedback: [["1/2", "3 − 5 = −2, so 2⁻² = 1/4."], ["-4", "A negative power isn't a negative number."]], explain: "2³ ÷ 2⁵ = 2⁻² = 1/4." } - hint: ["$6^0 = 1$.", "Then $2^{-2}$."] check: { type: answer, q: "Work out $6^0 \\times 2^{-2}$ as a fraction.", answer: "1/4", form: simplest, feedback: [["0", "6⁰ is 1, not 0."], ["1/24", "6⁰ = 1. Multiply 1 by 1/4."]], explain: "6⁰ = 1 and 2⁻² = 1/4." } smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Just the first part: what's $6^0$?", answer: 1, explain: "Anything to the power 0 is 1." } - hint: ["Multiply the indices: −1 × −3.", "A negative times a negative is positive."] check: { type: number, q: "Edge case: simplify $(2^{-1})^{-3}$. It's 2 to what power?", answer: 3, explain: "−1 × −3 = 3, so 2³ = 8." } ``` ### Dividing to negative ### With a zero ### Negative times negative ## Practise: mixed laws ```step stage: practise insight: "Using each law with negative and zero indices, mixed; the review keeps one Year 8 law fresh." tasks: - check: type: number q: "Simplify $3^{-4} \\times 3^{6}$. It's 3 to what power?" answer: 2 explain: "−4 + 6 = 2." - check: type: number q: "Simplify $7^{2} \\div 7^{-3}$. It's 7 to what power?" answer: 5 explain: "2 − (−3) = 5." - check: type: number q: "Simplify $(5^{-2})^{3}$. It's 5 to what power?" answer: -6 explain: "−2 × 3 = −6." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Just the indices: what's $-2 \\times 3$?", answer: -6, explain: "A negative times a positive is negative: −6." } - check: type: answer q: "Review: work out $10^3 \\times 10^{-5}$ as a decimal." answer: "0.01" form: simplified feedback: - ["0.001", "3 + (−5) = −2, so 10⁻² = 0.01."] explain: "10³ × 10⁻⁵ = 10⁻² = 0.01." ``` ### Multiply ### Divide ### Power of a power ### Review Powers of 10, from the Year 8 laws. ## Make: back to the phone ```step stage: make insight: "Coming back to the photos: writing the sizes as powers of 10 turns the question into a division of numbers and a division of powers." tasks: - hint: ["Write both in bytes.", "128 ÷ 4 and 10⁹ ÷ 10⁶."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A phone has 128 GB of storage. Each photo is 4 MB. Use powers of 10 to work out how many photos fit." steps: - ["$128 \\times 10^{9}$ bytes and $4 \\times 10^{6}$ bytes", "giga is 10⁹ and mega is 10⁶"] - ["$(128 \\times 10^{9}) \\div (4 \\times 10^{6})$", "storage divided by the size of a photo"] - ["$32 \\times 10^{3}$", "128 ÷ 4 = 32 and 10⁹ ÷ 10⁶ = 10³"] - ["32 000 photos", "multiply out"] answer: "32000" answerLabel: "Photos" feedback: - ["32", "That's 32 × 10³, with the 10³ left off."] - ["320000", "10⁹ ÷ 10⁶ = 10³ = 1000, not 10 000."] criteria: - "I wrote both sizes in bytes as numbers times powers of 10." - "I divided the numbers and then subtracted the indices." - "My answer is in the tens of thousands." explain: "(128 × 10⁹) ÷ (4 × 10⁶) = 32 × 10³ = 32 000." - check: type: number q: "A kilobyte is $10^3$ bytes and a gigabyte is $10^9$ bytes. A kilobyte is $10^{?}$ of a gigabyte. What's the index?" answer: -6 explain: "10³ ÷ 10⁹ = 10⁻⁶: a millionth." ``` ### The photos Back to the phone. Work it out on paper first, then type your answer. ### A kilobyte as a fraction Prefix sizes: [SI prefixes, BIPM](https://www.bipm.org/en/measurement-units/si-prefixes). (Phone makers sometimes use $2^{10}$ steps; this task uses the SI powers of 10.) **Also used in** - **Computing.** Storage, memory and download speeds all use kilo, mega, giga. - **Next lessons.** The same laws on letters, then scientific notation. ```teacher summary: Students use all the index laws with zero and negative indices, take care subtracting a negative, and work out how many photos fit on a phone from powers of 10 (AC9M9A01, node 2). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can simplify powers of the same base with negative and zero indices. - I can subtract a negative index correctly. - I can use powers of 10 to divide very big numbers. struggle: "Signs: subtracting a negative index. Ask students to write 6 − (−2) with the brackets before they work it out." before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need Negative powers and the Year 8 index laws. The one idea: the laws don't change; the care is in the signs. The common mistake is subtracting the size of a negative index (Jo's working). Prefix sizes (kilo 10³, mega 10⁶, giga 10⁹) are from the BIPM SI prefixes table. Phone storage in practice sometimes counts in 1024s: the lesson uses the SI powers of 10 and says so. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Those who chose 32 or 320 000 lost or added zeros." - "Run: ask students to say the index of the answer before they read it." - "Paper: the try-one after the worked example and the photos in Make are worked on paper first. Books out, and look for the indices written with brackets." - "Modify: before (2⁻¹)⁻³, ask whether the answer is bigger or smaller than 1." stuck: - see: A student writes 5⁶ ÷ 5⁻² = 5⁴. ask: What's 6 − (−2)? fix: 8. Subtracting a negative adds. - see: A student writes (5⁻²)³ = 5⁻⁵. ask: Do you add or multiply for a power of a power? fix: "Multiply: −2 × 3 = −6." stretch: How many kilobytes make a gigabyte? Work out 10⁹ ÷ 10³ and say what the index tells you. support: "A law card: product (add), quotient (subtract), power (multiply), with one example each." leads: > Continues AC9M9A01 node 2. Where it leads: index laws on letters (next), scientific notation, exponential decay (Year 10). exit: q: Simplify 4⁻² × 4⁵ ÷ 4⁻¹. a: 4⁴ = 256. explain: > The index laws work with any indices. Multiplying adds the indices, dividing subtracts them, and a power of a power multiplies them. Subtracting a negative adds: $5^6 \div 5^{-2} = 5^{6 - (-2)} = 5^8$. ```

# Jo's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: jo
Simplify 5⁶ ÷ 5⁻².
Same base, so subtract the indices.
6 − 2 = 4.
So 5⁶ ÷ 5⁻² = 5⁴.
# endregion
